capabilities: Display typographic characters for dashes, arrows, ellipses, and ranges in prose
Protect code, math, links, frontmatter, and Markdown structure from conversion
Shape regional CJK punctuation and curly quotes with script-aware fonts
Toggle rendering separately for Source Mode, Live Preview, Reading View, and print/PDF
Reveal original source tokens when the cursor enters a transformed token
disambiguation: Not a source formatter; it never rewrites Markdown text, only how tokens are displayed while the file stays untouched.
extras: Not yet listed in the Obsidian Community plugins directory, so it must be installed manually from GitHub releases. Free under the MIT license with no paid edition, telemetry, or advertising; architecture details live in ARCHITECTURE.md rather than the README.
problem: Obsidian shows literal source tokens like --, ..., and -> in prose and applies no publication-style typography or CJK punctuation shaping across its views.
summary: Typography renderer that displays publication-quality characters such as dashes, arrows, ellipses, and CJK punctuation without changing the Markdown source.
